references.text: God commands Noah to bring two of every living creature into the ark, male and female, to keep them alive during the flood.
Specifies that Noah is to take seven pairs of each clean animal and one pair of the unclean animals, as well as seven pairs of birds, to preserve their kinds on earth.
Confirms that the animals entered the ark with Noah in pairs, male and female, just as God had commanded Noah.
The Lord urges His people to enter their chambers and shut the doors behind them—a thematic parallel to how the Lord shut the ark after Noah to protect him.
By faith Noah built an ark to save his family, which condemned the world and made him an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
God did not spare the ancient world but preserved Noah, a preacher of righteousness, along with seven others when He brought the flood upon the ungodly—highlighting God's protection of Noah.
